reviews.comment: She's so bad don't take the class. Her lectures she just reads off slides. The exams are impossible to study for, no matter what you study you're going to fail
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very sweet, but the difficulty of her tests do not match her notes, homework, or practice problems. If you're an average student, prepare to not get anything higher than a C.
shes so nice.... aviod her at all costs

Dropped her class because it was lowk hard to keep up with the heavy workload. She also said she had never done 120 before (I took her in 2025) and that was already worrying to me. I will say she was very energetic and kind, which made lectures less boring. Compared to Dr. Barondeau, she wasn't great at explaining things and I would be very lost.
The HW is reasonable, but I think the exams were unnecessarily difficult. I would study for hours and still fail.

Prof. Altemose cares about her students; however, the content she taught was far too easy compared to the exams. Her lectures were engaging, but did not prepare you at all for exams. The homework is reasonable and is assigned on a weekly basis. Be ready to self study the entire class.

This professor cared a lot about the students and the class. However, I had to self teach myself almost all of the material. Her class is heavily based on the textbook and she rarely talks about it. Just make sure to use all of the resources available because learning from her alone is not enough, but she does curve at the end so that is nice.

Very sweet person, but her exams are pretty hard, and slideshows don't have enough room to do calculations. The textbook will be your best friend, so take separate notes from that. It's not impossible to pass if you put in the effort.

One of my least favorite professors in college. Take anyone else for 107, Martinez is supposed to be much better. Altemose quizzes are insanely hard for no reason like you will have to study so hard and get a 50 on a quiz. also quiz average matters because there is two tests and a final.

Altemose is a great professor and I know my grade doesn't show it. She does have harder tests but I would recommend going to office hours and trying to really understand the material. I wish that I had taken advantage of the office hours, SI Sessions, and the homework to learn the material. With Altemose she gives extra credit. Just put effort!

Amazing professor. CHEM 120 is a tough class but Dr. Altemose does her best to help every students in the course. She makes sure everyone can reach her outside of class, always gives extra credits for each exam, and very nice and dedicated to the students. She often stayed past her office hours to help the students as well.

Her lectures are very surface level. The examples she teaches are not what you will be seeing on your exams so be prepared to self educate on everything. Her reviews are absolutely appalling. Her handwriting is a complete mess and very often illegible. She's pretty easy to reach out to and provides resources to supplement her lack of teaching.

She is a very nice person however her exams are extremely hard. They make up the majority of your grade and aren't curved even if the average is very low. Her exams go into WAY more depth than her lectures go in class. If you can take another professor I would because she makes her exams way too hard for no reason.

Dr. A cares a lot about her students. Her lectures and notes provided enough information to understand all of the underlying concepts. The test questions were difficult but not impossible. My real issue is with the test structure where each question is weighted 7.78 pts/140 total. (Missing 2 questions is an 89), very little room for error.

Honestly, this professor is genuinely hard. The practice exams are much simpler than the real exams, which require deep thinking and strong understanding of concepts. Her lectures are not bad, but I had to self-study a lot. I earned an A, barely. A B is attainable if you study consistently, but expect difficult exams even when prepared.

Honestly, this professor is genuinely hard. The practice exams are much simpler than the real exams, which require deep thinking and strong understanding of concepts. Her lectures are not bad, but I had to self-study a lot. I earned an A, barely. An B is attainable if you study consistently, but expect difficult exams even when prepared.

Don't listen to all the bad reviews! She is so sweet and is always accessible. She got rid of quizzes this year and there are 1-2 short ALEKS due per week so it was not very time consuming out of lecture. Her exams are pretty difficult, but if you study the mock exams well and really grasp the conceptual stuff you will be fine!

20 points of extra credit, curved final grades at the end because class grade distribution was bad, exams were insanely hard but she's a nice person. Exams were almost always harder than the mock exams or quizzes provided, especially the final.

Super nice professor, but her exams are extremely difficult because they involve a level of deep understanding that is not required by most other classes. If you have taken Chem before and understand how each equation relates to one another and can understand things conceptually you will probably do fine, and she does give 20 points of extra credit

She's very nice and does care but just isn't the best at teaching. Tests unnecessarily hard a lot of the time, spends lots of time in lecture going into too much detail on stuff that doesn't need it and not enough time on what does. Aleks homework due every Monday, virtually pointless as it doesn't reflect tests

Altemose is a nice professor but DO NOT TAKE HER. Her lectures are only surface level and do not help for the exams at all. If you have to take her the best thing you can do is eat sleep and breathe mock exams and PowerPoint questions that she does not go over in lecture. Everything you study for the final will not be on the final.

Altemose is a nice professor, but her lectures are nowhere near the exams, and they touch only surface level. DO NOT TAKE HER. If you have to, the best thing you can do is memorize mock exams and do the questions on the power point until it's all you can think about. No matter what you study for the final, it will not be on the final.
Over 100+ Q-Drops this semester. Do I need to say anything else?

Take anybody else. Yes she's sweet and allows students to come up with names for her calves. It doesn't change the fact that her exams are harder than any other professor. If you dream of professional school, abandon all hope.

Tests are significantly harder than material taught in class, as well as the little study material that is given. Lectures are pure rambling. I would recommend taking any other prof than her until she realizes her tests are too difficult for how little she teaches, (which I don't think is any time soon considering her poor averages and no curves).

CHEM 120 is not an easy class, but Dr. Altemose teaches it well. I found that the exams were pretty similar to the practice exams, with some questions being the exact same and the overarching content being very similar. There was plenty of opportunity to get both participation credit and extra credit.

Taking Chem 120 later is better than how badly this class will tank your GPA. She is so sweet but exams are insanely difficult and makeup a majority of your grade. She also doesn't provide a lot of study material. Please don't take her if possible.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is so nice. However, I have never struggled so hard with a class. Her exams are just so hard. The highest grade I got was an 80 and I studied so hard, went to office hours, and tutoring. If you somewhat know what you are doing with chemistry you will probably be fine if you're willing to work for it. I would find someone else if you can.

She goes super fast, always felt like we were behind which definitely stressed me out a little. She's truly a really nice person but just not the best professor. Practice exams were far easier than the actual exams, all MCQ and no FRQ or partial credit, super test heavy in that sense.

Dr. Altemose is overall a good prof, but her tests are very hard. It feels a little unfair compared to other profs, so I would not necessarily recommend. If you do have her, she is super kind and really cares about the students. She is very accessible and is always willing to help you. Take advantage of her resources!
Tests are hard and it's unfair compared to the other profs

very nice prof but does not teach well, the exams are very difficult, if u want to do good it is important for you to do a LOT of self-studying but if you are able to switch out of her class, please do.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I cannot stress it enough, READ THE TEXTBOOK IN ALEKS! Her slide shows are very surface-level; the textbook helps you prepare for the depth of her exams. Exams are extremely difficult, and the only place you see similar questions is the practice quiz and practice exam. Study those and ask chat to make questions of similar difficulty! Very kind prof
Not always great at communicating course content but very obviously cares and willing to help

sweetest thing, could easily reach her through office hours or group me. lectures were all over the place. her mock + practice exams were nowhere near her actual exams. i averaged a 40 on them and wasn't about to risk my gpa. just an overall hard class, im sure there's other professors you can take. but again you will receive the effort you put in

You can tell that Dr. Altemose is very kind cares about her students, but her tests are just way too difficult for the depth we go into during class. She is infamous for giving the most difficult CHEM 120 tests in the department and doesn't teach well enough to justify their difficulty. Do not take her unless you're prepared for VERY rigorous exams

Dr. A is a very kind person, but a bad teacher. She lectures very surface level material, but her exams are extremely difficult. I studied for multiple weeks before the exams and tried a new method every time, but still failed to succeed. I dropped because in the end, the highest grade I could get was a C and I didn't want it to tank my GPA.

She is very sweet and truly cares about students, but her exams are so, so difficult. I think she is simply figuring out how to teach this class well, but most everyone from my lab group is dropping the class. If you want a good grade and chemistry is not your strength, I would find another prof to take.

Honestly, I think these ratings are too harsh for her. Sure, I wouldn't take her again but it's a very doable A as long as you put the work in. Exams aren't impossible, but they do require deep level understanding of the content to be able to apply. Go to office hours and ask her questions to fill in any gaps bc she's very receptive there!

Her exams are insane. No curves offered or anything. It is genuinely so unfair that our exams are harder than the rest of 120. The only reason she has a 2.9 and not a 1 on here is because she is a nice lady. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS.

Do. Not. Take. Her. Her exams are outrageous and no other chem 120 class has exams this hard. My friends who have different chem 120 profs are genuinely shocked when I show them our exams. No curving at all. She's such a sweet person, but her exams make me feel like she must hate us like I don't get it.

Do not take her, her lectures are alright, but genuinely, the exams are so hard. I would tell my friends about our exams, and they were in the same course but with different professors who made the exams not as hard. She also doesn't curve at all, even if the class performs poorly on exams, which I'm still confused about. Good luck.

The lectures are not engaging, and the material covered is a lot easier than the exam. I would recommend learning additional information on your own and using the problems in the textbook to study.  She is accessible outside of class which is convenient.

She's sweet but makes literally the hardest tests in the entire course. All of my friends with other profs have looked at our mock exams and said they are insane. Offers ~ 20 points extra credit, but the tests are so difficult it doesn't really matter. No curving or bumping. Take ANYONE else, I thought I would be able to manage but ig not!!
This class is insane. Exams are nothing like the practice ones. I feel like I can not keep up in lecture, her slides are very unorganized.

Mock exams are not like actual exams and you need to know concepts and how to do all the formulas with your eyes closed. She introduces new concepts with a minute left in lecture. Office hours are not helpful unless you have very specific questions. She is very sweet to talk to, but very hard class.
Dont take care. Lectures barely make sense but the tests are extremely difficult for absolutely no reason.

I personally found her lectures very useful, especially early on in the semester.  The second and final exams were fairly difficult. The questions on the exams are very different then the questions on the homework problems and she only posts one practice exam.

Her exams are ridiculously difficult compared to what she teaches in lecture. I had an A in Chem 119 and still cannot pass her exams. The examples she teaches are easy, but the test questions are on a completely different level. She also rushes lectures and introduces new concepts with a minute of class left. Avoid her.

Please avoid this professor at all costs. Lectures are disorganized and rushed. She gives extra credit quizzes and practice tests that you think would help, but just like the lecture material, they are very surface level. Exams are well over 50% of your overall grade and they are incredibly difficult and nothing like the lectures. Thumbs down :(
Her lectures weren't useful. She rushed through them and didn't really teach. Other than that, quizzes and tests seemed to have some topics that we didn't learn about.

Dr. Altemose is a great person. She seems very caring and genuinely wants you to do your best and succeed in the class. Classes however were very hard to follow and feel like the slides are being rushed rather than actually taught. 
The content on quizzes and tests often feels like it comes out of nowhere, not taught with the lecture material.

She is a really nice person and very accessible, whether that be in office hours or GroupMe, but her lectures are not very helpful. The lectures are pretty surface level while tests and quizzes are more difficult in my opinion. The homework would take hours, and they were also pretty difficult. Overall she is kind but doesn't teach the course well.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. A was the most caring professor I had and super accessible outside of class on GroupMe. I found her lectures and slides to be great and helpful for the tests, though make sure you know the material well, especially for her quizzes which can be tough. I came in with just 10th grade chem knowledge and didn't find it overly difficult to get an A.

Teaching quality is weak, with lectures moving too fast and slides clicked through instead of explained. Concepts are not broken down well, leaving students to self-teach. The course is very exam-heavy with difficult, heavily weighted questions. BUT she is genuinely kind and wants students to succeed.
Insanely hard exams.

Dr. A is a great person who truly cares about her students. Her office hours are pretty helpful, and she is always talking about the Chemistry Learning Lab. Definitely use these resources because there is a lot of information to cover and on occasion she wouldn't explain the concepts well enough.

She's not the best lecturer but she's super accessible via GroupMe for any questions. She's passionate about chemistry, patient, kind, and whimsical. Please don't leave lecture early -- she always sounds sad when people start filing out with 5 minutes left. You definitely have a lot of self-teaching to look forward to, though.

I took Professor Altemose for CHEM107 for Fall 2025. You need a really solid foundation in Chemistry to succeed, and even then I found it tough get an A. Yes, she's good, but CHEM107 is a real pain. We did random stuff for participation points, so you have to show up for every lecture, because you just can't take a risk with your grade.

Dr.Altemose is really nice and carrying. I was hoping to get an A or B in the course but the final is long and hard so LOCK IN a few weeks before! If this course is not mandatory for your degree I'd highly suggest taking 119 or 120, they are better suited for non-engineers! She's always accessible and helpful so make sure to go to office hours!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, she is a very caring professor and also very accessible outside of class. The lecture slides could be a little confusing at times. She doesn't do a particularly amazing job at connecting the concepts, just kind of throwing them out there. The tests are the toughest out of any prof, but she also makes up for it with a curve.

Dr. A is a very caring professor with poor time management in lectures. If you're taking the time to understand the content and homework on your own you'll be fine. A lot of the difficultly of the class comes from the grading policies and lack of time spent on difficult concepts. Approach the class like math and learn to solve problems.

She is a very kind and supportive professor who offers many resources to help students succeed. However, the exams and quizzes were very challenging, and compared to other sections, they felt noticeably harder. The class has participation points, and the lectures can be somewhat unengaging.

While she is very caring, that doesn't help your grade! Lectures are all over the place and do not match the info in the test. She asked us to watch an hours worth of videos over the break since she didn't have time to cover it in class. Also gives the hardest tests out of any 107 professor. The only good thing is the detailed feedback on quizzes.

Overall, this course is not bad if you have taken chemistry before. I took AP Chemistry and got a 4, and I BARELY got an A in this class. The quizzes are hard, and the exams are pretty tough as well. I would say the best thing to do is go over the lecture slides before the lecture, and study the material a little bit everyday. Goodluck buddy.

There are a lot of overly negative reviews but in general the best advice for her class is to do the homeworks. The exam/quiz questions are pretty much pulled from them verbatim. She isn't a bad prof but her SI does need to be replaced. Don't waste your time going over her slideshow when studying tho. hoemwork,quiz,exammockmuchbetter.

Dr. Altemose is sweet and accessible, but her teaching is inadequate. Lectures were confusing and incomplete. Her own quizzes and exams were drastically different and more complex than the lecture, homework, and practice exam. Other professors' quizzes and exams were simpler. She didn't do extra credit, but she curved 2 points to a passing grade.
She is really sweet, but her class is just so difficult.

I put a lot of time into preparing for quizzes and exams, but they felt unnecessarily hard. Compared to mock exams from other professors, this class was much tougher. Her lectures didn't help me learn. While she cares about students, the workload felt unfair without common exams for chem 107.
Dr. Altemose is horrible at teaching bro. We did nothing productive other than name cows. She glosses over things way too quick and doesn't care for our understanding.

Lectures are big nothing burgers that don't cover the information you need. Do the homework and understand to the big picture and you'll do fine. She would explain simple topics in the worst ways that actually make things way harder to understand. 99% of the time just ignore what she says and find your own way to go about the problems and concepts.

The class itself is a lot, there's so much material to cover and the professor does really well in going over everything that needs to be covered. Yes sometime she rushes at the end but if you ever have questions she will sit with you one on one and help you understand things better. Show up to office hours, ask questions.

I've never ONCE met a teacher so unbelievably TERRIBLE at teaching. Her lectures are messy slogs to go through (Some presentations had 100+ slides) and she does an AWFUL job at pacing herself. HW takes HOURS of time to complete while quizzes & exams significantly more difficult. Use Chad's Prep to (On YT) & pray if end up in her class...

A lot of people complain that Dr. Altemose's lectures aren't helpful, but its not her its the class itself. She does her best to make the lectures entertaining, does small cool experiments at the end of class. Her quizzes are very hard, but they prepare you very well for the common exams. But she does sometimes not explain some concepts on the exam
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take her.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes were unnecessarily difficult sometimes; She just makes the class harder than it needs to be. She has poor time management so she starts the class off really slow and then by the end she skips through a bunch of important slides and rushes the information so that we can kind of do the homework. She was nice though.

She is so caring.  You can tell she loves chemistry and wants to see her students succeed. She isn't the greatest at explaining difficult concepts, but she gives so many opportunities to see her and learn.  The bad reviews make her look way worse than she is; they just want a pushover who will give them an easy A.
very good!

She is a very nice person and that personality was fun to see during the lectures. But she was quite poor teaching during lectures and would often take too much time explaining some concepts and then just completely gloss over other concepts. Some concepts were even easier to learn outside of class than just based on her lectures. Mediocre overall

Chem 107 is hard period. But oh my god she is not good at explaining concepts and skips over the important stuff so quickly. She is so nice but it is so hard to pay attention during her lectures as she draws on unimportant material for so long. I would highly suggest going to the Chemistry Learning Lab if you can't get another professor to study.

abandon all hope all ye who take this class, terrible lecturer; doesn't teach material very well, sometimes homeworks due before she actually goes over the material and when she does she'll cover one practice problem and ramble on about the next chapter or things that aren't gonna be on the test.

Dr. Altemose's lectures were extremely fast and confusing for me, But I think this is a result of the course and not the teacher. She is AMAZING in her office hours and extremely accessible in her GroupMe. This class was extremely difficult for me, but she is very willing to help you through the tough material. Don't be swayed by her bad ratings.

I can definitely tell that she tries to be the best she could. I think she is a very friendly professor and tries her best to make her lectures make sense but as someone who has taken AP chem before, I feel like people who hasn't done so would feel very lost in her class.
she's really nice don't get me wrong but girl bye just take someone else bro

Just no. Her quizzes were unnecessarily difficult with a consistent intention to mess you up on every question.
As a person, she was very kind and quirky, she is not evil. But as a professor, she kind of is.

Dr. Altemose is a nice person. I had a terrible time while in her class. Her lectures were always a slog and at that same time still wouldn't cover enough. Tests were difficult but similar to her mock exams. The worst part of class was her homework. Takes literal hours and goes over redundant/non quiz and exam material on occasion. Overall, Awful.

Her lectures are a trillion slides. She will spend 6 minutes talking, then say it's not on the test, and then have to rush to complete the notes. The quizzes and tests are way too short for what they are. And sometimes the homework will go over content that isn't on the test, or never taught, and they all take hours.

Chem 107's a common course but one area of improvement would be to find a new SI leader. The SI leader for fall 2025 gave the impression she really didn't care about her job and was forced to be there. Not only that but you'd be scared to ask her questions when it's an SI session and answering student questions is the whole point of those.
Horrible tests, boring lectures. Doesn't prepare well

Left during the middle of the hardest test content for a week. Her Pop Quizzes were closed note and worth a good percentage of the grade, and they were harder than the exams. That being said, her exams were VERY hard! While she was gone, Professor Mawk guest lectured, and he said our slide content was too hard for our level. Tests were harder..
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. A herself is a very kind professor, however with the amount of content in the course and its structure, it's very hard to ever feel prepared. I used the mock exams as a study tool, and while the exam was similar, it included a ton of unnecessary extra steps that I had neither the time or understanding to do effectively.

While an extremely nice and understand person, my experience was not the best in the classroom setting. There would be many times we would learn something in class than get a long email afterwards saying she explained it wrong and this was the actual way to do it. The quizzes were HARDER than the exams, and those were also extremely hard. DONT TAKE

She is a very kind person and is very easy to talk to and she tries her best to help as much as she can. But the class is so hard, and her quizzes and tests are much harder than whatever she teaches. Additionally, it is annoying because the other professors have easier quizzes and exams, and others do better with less effort.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Altemose is so kind. She cares about her students so much. She is extremely accommodating and will work with you. Her lectures are clear and easy to follow. Chem 119 is not a fun or easy class, but if you have to take it, take it with Altemose.

Dr A was kind and accessible outside of class; however, her lectures were very disorganized & hard to follow. The exams were very difficult, much more advanced than what is to be expected of Gen Chem. Beware of quizzes which are timed & entirely FRQ. I have never struggled with Chem until now and that seems to be a popular sentiment among students.

Yeah I failed 120. Part of that was me not getting myself enough help. I am not chemistry-ily inclined but almost got a B in 119. Major: POSC-technical.       Dr A was a pleasant prof but VERY confusing (a lot of my classmates said so too). She's great for everything except lectures - those are basically useless. You'll need another source of info.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult and hard to follow. She writes all over the board in a very disorganized way during lecture. The tests, like others have said, are designed to separate the pass and fails - not much in between. Also, her 3 exams are 16 QUESTIONS! You do the math if you get just a couple wrong...
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All these reviews are probably people who weren't used to putting in a little effort in a class. If you're hardworking and can follow some lecture slides and do the harder problems of each weeks homework and review the quizzes and mock exams she gives, the tests are essentially the exact same. She gives quite a bit of extra credit and is caring.

Dr. A as a person is very sweet. As a professor, however, stay away. Her lectures were scatterbrained and had tons of mistakes, as did the homework and tests (the final alone had at least three mistakes). I taught myself the material and passed because I learned how to take her tests. Overall frustrating and unacceptable for a "top tier" university

Actual stats for Chem 120 (edited 5/20) without the averages of her other courses, because the overall professor rating is not relevant.

Average Quality Rating: 1.95 / 5

Average Difficulty Rating: 4.58 / 5

Take into account ppl who got good grades are the ones giving the good reviews. Then, even ppl with As and Bs left negative reviews.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ignore all the bad reviews, I'm convinced it's people who didn't get the grade they wanted. She genuinely cares about her students and was accessible outside of class. Additionally, she's a very fair grader and often gave partial credit or extra credit. You do have to pay attention in lecture; she won't just give you the answers. Do mock exams too!

I struggle to find out what to say about her... she often messes up things in lecture and can be very confusing sometimes. Her quizzes and tests are tough but can be manageable if you work hard. No matter what people say, the mock exams have the same format as the exams but just know the info. Overall not the best, but she is very nice and caring.

Dr. A fumbles through lectures like she's reading off a bad script, constantly screwing up and wasting everyone's time. Her exams are a chaotic mess with impossible questions meant to fail you, not teach you. Taking her class is signing up for a nightmare—avoid like the plague.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very thorough lectures (can be a lot of info). She was super open to meeting outside class to discuss grade concerns. Relatively hard exams/final but thats more due to the class itself. I had no previous chem knowledge and struggled for an A. Altemose probably gave a small curve at the end of the sem which saved my grade. Hard class but nice prof!

She is a very sweet and caring person. But she is not meant to teach 120, she knows about 107 but not 120. She has no idea what she's doing, but still managed to have the hardest exams possible. You have to self teach yourself for this class. It's really sad because she really does try and is very nice, but can't teach this class to save her life.

Took her for 107 and thought she was great and chem was just hard so took her again for 120 but quickly realized that a good portion of the difficulty came from her teaching methods and unreasonably difficult quizzes and exams. Don't get me wrong, she's super sweet and caring but please do not make that the reason you take her.

Notice how even the 5 star reviews don't disregard how hard exams and quizzes are. The good reviews are saying you just need to put in a little extra work to get a B, but putting in 20+ hours for a single exam to barely scrape a B/C is diabolical and should be a wake up call to make exams easier. Save your time and gpa and just take another prof.

Altemose is a very caring and kind professor, but she needs some work on her preparation coming into CHEM 120 (especially her lectures). Her quizzes and exams are very difficult so I would study accordingly and ahead of time. Go to the CLL and do all the extra credit given.

Dr. A is a nice person and was always accessible outside of class. However, lectures were disorganized, quizzes were impossible to pass, and exams were only moderately similar to mock exams and homework. It is not impossible to get a B, but be prepared to put all your effort into studying for just this class.

Prof A is a decent professor and I would say cares for her students. She did make some mistakes in lectures, but they were fixable, especially if reviewing with outside sources. There is just so little room for error on quizzes/exams, which makes the class harder than 119. I averaged LOW on quizzes and high on exams for a fair B.

what i got in class: i averaged a 50 on the exams, including the lab assessment and final. i completed all of the homeworks, went to most classes, and averaged a 72 on quizzes. I passed with a 70. It's really hard to fail this class. The professor isn't that bad. There's a lot of homework. Quizzes are hard. But it's doable, since theres a lot of EC

I've seen a lot of 5 and 1 reviews, but she is probably somewhere in the middle. It is true that she left the country right before one of the exams and q-drop with no warning, which is why some people have her rated lower. You can do good, but it is MUCH harder than 119. Be prepared to fail at least 1-2 quizzes and underperform on at least 1 exam.

I think her lectures were good. Also her exams weren't that hard. For ex, a question I specifically noticed as hard on exam 3 was literally on the homework. The quizzes were hard, but not ALL of them. A few easier ones were present for balance. The quizzes were harder than the exams, good preparation.

Dr. A is a nice lady, but she struggles to explain material and answer questions, often creating confusion in class. Not a good option for people who already struggle with chem. Her exams are notoriously difficult (even acknowledged by another chem prof), and she doesn't curve. Sometimes there's partial credit though, and she provides mock exams.

Altemose is an okay professor, but if you can get into another professor's class, I would HIGHLY recommend doing that. She asks questions on the quizzes and tests that are confusing and completely different than the questions she has gone over in class and on the homework. Achievable to get an A but a lot of work and self-teaching is required.
Save your gpa pls, don't take her. Got an A in chem 119, but struggled extremely in this course.

I came into chem 120 already having this credit from ap chem & I still struggled in the class. Her exams & quizzes are RLLY hard and require an in-depth understanding of concepts she doesn't rlly prepare you for. I would understand all the HW, lectures, & practice problems & still do bad on exams bc the questions were WAY beyond what we covered.

Lectures = somewhat confusing, She skips through the slides and doesn't do example problems worth your time. Exams are 16 questions no partial credit (unless majority fails). Quizzes are near impossible to pass. She seems like she cares, but her actions do not show it. On the other hand, very responsive after class and willing to answer Qs
Very nice, but the tests are a lot harder than those of other professors, and she seems very new to the material

Don't come into Chem 120 if you don't plan on studying more. Obviously, the mock exams are going to be different than the actual exams or she'd just be giving you the answers. The quizzes are difficult. If you learn ALL the underlying concepts, you'll soon realize that her class isn't impossible. Take these reviews with a grain of salt.

Chemistry is not a subject that can just be memorized. That is why everyone thinks her exams are impossible to pass (many people did just fine). Instead of doing practice problems until you can answer a question any way it's given, people are blaming the professor. College is about learning. Find a new study method and take accountability.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think all the bad reviews are coming from Dr. A's first time teaching chem 120. Even though it was her 1st time, I thought her lectures were pretty good and enthusiastic. My only complaint is that the quizzes were sometimes difficult. If you thoroughly understand every practice problem in class and don't chat the HW, you will be prepared.

DUDE. LITERALLY NO OMG. JUST TOOK THE FINAL. NEVER AGAIN. If you want to take her, I would rethink that. She doesnt show you your grade till ur done with the class (the grade calculator literally suck and so confusing to use so dont even bother) THE EXAMS ARE SO HARD. Every test ive taken i have looked over and saw someone either crying or about to

This class was a real struggle. The lectures were confusing, and the she made mistakes during class that added to the difficulty. I learned far more in SI and IA sessions than I ever did in class. The quizzes were very challenging, and the homework didn't match the difficulty or style of the exams, which made it hard to know what to expect.
If you aren't religious, pick one and pray.

I took her for Chem 120. DO NOT MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE!!!! If you enjoy feeling more lost after attending a lecture, take her class. Tests and quizzes are outrageous. Save your GPA and take literally anyone else. Who knows, maybe she will take two weeks off with 1 day's notice before an impossible exam(actually happened). Good luck!
she locked all of our quizzes before our final :(

I do not reccomend this class, Dr. Atlemos is a great person but her test difficulty and quizzes are very hard. I got an A in Chem 119, but failed almost every quiz and exam in this class. She has the overall grade locked too so you are never sure what you have minus the calculators she posts where you have to estimate every future grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't deserve all the hate she gets. She's made a few mistakes in class, but the main thing is that one of her exams was extremely difficult and her quizzes are close to impossible to do well on. Doing good on the exams makes up for the quizzes and as long as you pay attention in class and do the extra credit, a B should be very attainable.

this was just the worst. prof A is SO SWEET, but her teaching capabilities were subpar. tests were IMPOSSIBLE, if you don't study a week + in advance, your'e cooked. quizzes with webcam were SO hard too. not sure why she made everything so hard like ???. ik chem is tough, but she made it unbearable & miserable tbh :( she's so nice though

Skipped through half the notes and seemed to expect students to know how to do everything. Was usually all over the place when lecturing and would get lost in her own work. Office hours were okay at best. Homework takes hours upon hours of work.

I took Professor Altemose Fall 2023. While I don't remember the exact details, I can say that she was a good lecturer. Many people here are complaining about how she only gave a final review if 75% of the class completed the AEFIS course evaluation, but no professor is obligated to give a final review. Besides that, I have no complaints.

She's only giving a final exam review if 75% of the class completes the course evaluation. She's prioritizing her feedback over her students learning and success. If helping students really matters, a final review session shouldn't be conditional and should be offered no matter what. This says all you need to know about taking her class.

Dr. A is a sweet lady with a caring personality, but her chem 120 class is near to impossible. She was confused on her own material, and often taught us the wrong way. She rushed through notes as if we already knew how to do these very complex problems. I went to SI and got a tutor, and the exams were horrible. I do not recommend taking her.

Dr. A's class is a rollercoaster of confusion, and the almost biweekly quizzes are the true loop-de-loops. Lockdown browser + webcam = constant stress, like they're watching you fail in real time. Lectures are a mix of mistakes and surprise concepts, and exams feel like a game of “Guess What She Meant.” Sweet lady, but this class is a nightmare.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. A is very nice, however DONT TAKE HER CLASS. She is completely all over the place when teaching and her exams are IMPOSSIBLE to pass. If only she would teach from a students perspective instead of assuming that everyone is already an expert. PLEASE IF YOU CAN TAKE SOMEONE ELSE DO SO.
Never had a professor so messy at teaching.

Overall she is a good person, but she is terrible at teaching. She goes by fast on the lectures and expects us to already know everything. Her exams are really hard and even her study guides are not similar to the exams.

In my opinion, she is not someone who cares one bit. She seems to get pleasure knowing people struggle in her class, and knows students are critiquing her on RMP but even then refuses to look at it because it'll "make her sad" instead of seeing what she can do to improve. Never have I studied 20 hrs for exams and failed (she'll trick you on them).

Dr. Altemose seems like a genuinely nice person, but not a great professor unfortunately. The homework she assigns is not aligned with what ends up on quizzes and exams (btw 7.5 pts. per question and only 16 Qs on exams-do the math). She left in the middle of the semester to another country with NO prior notice and returned day of Q-Drop.

I have never been so lost in a class before. I swear she also doesn't know what she is talking about and messes up at least once each lecture. She makes quizzes and tests way harder than they need to be. And lab won't help either because guess what, SHES HEAD OF THE DEPARTMENT AND MADE THE LAB TEST IMPOSSIBLE. Don't take.

She doesn't prepare you for the exams at all. Lectures don't match what's on the test and there's barely any helpful practice. Every test and quiz was basically a jump scare, nothing like what she gives you in class, on iclickers, or ALEKS.

She is so horrible. I have never had a professor so hard to follow and disorganized. Her exams are so difficult and her material will not prepare you. From the first exam to the end it feels like you're drowning and you have to teach yourself everything. I genuinely don't think she could pass her own exams.
Future students: spend time reading the textbook, going over notes, and reviewing homework instead of spending all your time on RMP and you will succeed :)

Do not take this professor. Exams are difficult and nothing like the practice quizzes/exams. 
Quizzes are taken online; quite unforgiving. Made Chemistry harder than it needed to be.

If you ever want a chance of leaving chem 120 with your sanity PLEASE take anyone else. She is horrifyingly bad at lecturing and leaves you more confused. Exams are at level impossible, so good luck even trying to get a B. She makes me question my will to live after every class.  She created the worlds hardest exam then left the country for 2 weeks

PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD TAKE ANYONE ELSE!! Dr.A is the WORSE professor iv'e ever had. She seems completely unaware of her own content and makes so so many mistakes during lecture that leaves me more confused then when I started. Don't even think she knows what she is teaching half the time. I leave every lecture feeling confused, and worthless
It's just an L, I promise. Look at the other reviews, I'm not the only one.

Dr. A is a very sweet lady, but I had a lot of trouble learning in her class despite going to every lecture and spending countless hours studying. She is good at writing really hard exams, and if you aren't a natural at chemistry, you will struggle with her. The assignments and lab aren't enough cushion if you do poorly on her exams/quizzes.

Very sweet person, however her exams are fairly different and often harder than any of the other material in the class, which makes them difficult to prepare for. Lectures are fairly boring and hard to sit through, but she posts them after the fact which helps. Would be a much more manageable class if the exams matched the mocks more closely.

I am disappointed to see some reviews bashing our professor and am surprised to see that many of my peers seem to be lacking accountability. She is kind, very easily reachable outside of class, and always willing to help. In my opinion, chem is a difficult course, but needing to put in some extra study time doesn't mean your professor isn't good.
Very hard tests that she doesn't prepare you for. I even had a tutor and understood the material but still only made 70s on her test. If you want an A/B in chem then do not take her.

She's a very sweet woman, but her lectures were extremely confusing and unorganized, imo. You could practice with SI, the practice exam, and through ALEKS and STILL fail. I pray for whoever gets her. But, again, she's a nice lady.

Mrs. Altemose's class is where curiosity goes to die. Her lectures are dull, her explanations are wrong 50% of the time, and her exam's like stepping into the Nether in Minecraft without any resources. Chemistry becomes a fog of confusion under her instruction. If learning is a spark, she's the extinguisher. She transforms science into suffering.

Whatever you do, do NOT take Altemose. By far the WORST chem instructor I've ever had. Constantly confused, never has answers, says she'll “google it and send an announcement later.”Exams and quizzes are outrageous & nothing like lectures. She left the country mid sem with 0 notice. Absolute chaos. Save yourself the MISERY and find a better prof.

For some reason everyone thinks a 70% average for a 400 person class in gen chem is bad, when that's probably on the high side. I've never been in a lecture this big with an exam average over 75. Also, she's coming back before the q drop date, she didn't just “leave out of nowhere.”

Dr.A seems like a super sweet lady, but you have to do a lot of teaching yourself out of class. Her in-class clicker and practice problems are straightforward and so are the ALEKS hw. The quizzes are pretty rough and they are timed. You are going to have to use ALL offered resources to be successful on the exams. The mock exam isn't enough.

She left the country before our third exam and Q-drop deadline. The average for our exam was a 70% with a curve. She has the canvas grader off and her grade calculator is not accurate. Many people Q-dropped and she didn't come back a day before the last Q-drop date. Her bonus points won't improve your overall score. Do with the info what you will.
Messes up occasionally during her lectures, doesn't need to make quizzes lockdown browser + webcam, and definitely could make tests longer than 16 questions.

Pick another prof. Quizzes are such an inconvenience and they're hard, and exams are worse. Her exam reviews do not prepare you at all and it feels like she's pulling questions out of nowhere and then expects us to know it. Doesn't curve either. Makes lots of mistakes in class as well then laughs it off like our grades aren't the ones suffering.
Makes an exam so hard even other profs are surprised by. *leaves the country

Let me be honest: Dr. A makes this course way harder than it needs to be. She doesn't adequately teach the material compared to other profs. Almost everyone runs out of time on quizzes and exams and leaves feeling discouraged. Even as someone who studies daily and has a 4.0, I've struggled greatly. Dr. A is sweet, but seriously don't take her.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She cares a lot about the students yet she doesn't explain the best but overall she prepares you pretty well for the exams. Exams are 16 questions but almost identical to the mock exams she gives you in far advance. Quizzes are the hardest will little questions but they are very close to the examples on the slides. Definitely would take her again.
The worst professor I have ever had. I will most likely have to take this class again to get a better grade because it is mandatory for my degree plan. STAY FAR FAR AWAY!!!!

I'm pretty conflicted with Professor Altemose. Chem 120 is definitely a step up from 119, which I loved. I had imo the best professor at a&m, professor Karim Afroz for 119, so going from her to Prof Altemose was a significant decline in teaching. She is a very nice lady, but her lectures are very subpar and tests are difficult. Do not recommend.

1 star is dramatic but she's def not a 5 star prof. Her lecture material does NOT reflect the difficulty of the exam and I put in the work. She makes a LOT of mistakes in lectures. Her quizzes are ROUGH. She gives so many resources so takes advantage of them! They help but not enough to prepare you for exam lvl. TBH don't ignore low April reviews.
She doesn't teach very well, don't take this class! The real tests are nothing like her actual exams.

She isn't a bad teacher. However, the course is extremely rigorous. There are few opportunities to increase your grade outside of exams. She instead of replacing an exam grade she averages the final with it which is extremely frustrating. This class has no room for forgiveness and if you're not perfect expect to drop it. Simply: Take another class.

Please do not take Dr. Altemos for Chem 120! She is a really sweet, kind person and accessible out of class, her course is still very difficult. Her tests only have 16 questions and are EXTREMELY hard to pass. Her mock exams, practice, and hw don't adequately prepare you for exams. Her 6 quizzes are mini exams and definitely not grade boosters.

IGNORE THE PEOPLE TELLING YOU TO IGNORE THE BAD REVIEWS. Dr.A isn't a 1star prof but she's most definitely not a 5. She sometimes doesn't know what she's doing and confuses the class, making things more difficult than they are. Her exams are difficult but not impossible.

IGNORE APRIL 2025 REVIEWS. Everyone's mad about a hard exam because it was different from the practice and she was out of the country. This DOESN'T negate how wonderful she is. While this is a hard class and she makes human mistakes, she cares for her students. Posts notes and kind. Out of what's available for 120 she's one of the better options.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This review bombing after the third exam is ridiculous. Altemose has given us every opportunity to succeed, from constant responses on GroupMe to filled notes. Everyone talking about “mistakes during class” is referring to maybe two times that ever happened, and she's made up for it. She's great, don't let unprepared people's reviews sway you.

I am very disappointed to see this review bombing after our third exam. So many of these terrible ratings are reactionary responses to these scores. Dr. A gives so many opportunities to learn, and is incredibly caring. She's an amazing prof, and if she's reading these I hope she knows that these ratings DO NOT reflect reality.
This class makes me feel worthless. Take anyone else.

Dr. Altemose seems like a nice person but not a great prof. Her practice problems on IClicker and the lectures definitely don't resemble the difficulty level of the tests and quizzes. She has zooms and office hours to help but the main issue is that the tests are short and worth a lot but not enough similar practice problems are provided.

Dr. A is really nice, which is why it's so unfortunate her lecturing for CHEM120 has been sub-par. While she has given us a few extra credit opportunities and does partial credit on some of the MCQ, it doesn't make up for how difficult the quizzes and exams are. I LOVED 119, so it's been really discouraging. Take someone else — Zhu if teaching.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The hw, in class practice problems, and practice exam are always so much easier than the actual exam, it feels like you're going in blind. Not enough practice problems at the rigor of the exam.

Avoid. Tests and quizzes don't match lectures. She doesn't just substitute numbers like another reviewer said. Leaving her students hanging with no support to jet to Australia tells you all you need to know about how much she prioritizes her students. Save your sanity--take someone else.

I dont want to write this because she cares about her students but Altemose is not great for 120. Don't get me wrong she's not the worst, take her over Mawk or Songok. Quizzes are ROUGH and tests are harder than practice exams or homework. She only curves if no one got 100. This is a weed out class (HARD) and you will be teaching yourself with her

I can see a lot of people think Altemose's class is hard, and I agree, I will absolutely concede that. There is very limited bonus, you need to attend lecture, the exams are time limited and each question has heavy weight. My issue is that the exam questions are just like the quiz, homework, and practice exam questions, just with different numbers.

Do not take her, she goes over content in class but the test are 10 times harder than the material she shares during lecture. Vey nice lady, but not a good professor for CHEM 120. In addition, her quizzes are free response and you only one day to complete them. They are also with lock down browser with video monitoring.

WHATEVER YOU DO, DO NOT TAKE HER!!!!! Very nice lady, but awful professor. Constantly makes mistakes in class, which confuses students even more. When this happens she tells us she will google the answer and send it to us. LIKE WHAT?! Spends too much time talking about her cows and not about material. STAY FAR AWAY!!!

SHE IS BUNSSSSS. Altemoses's Exams are so chopped, and she doesn't even know what she is teaching half the time. Multiple times in class, she did the problems wrong and told us to forget it and that she would post the updated slide later. Just don't take her, and if you can, switch out.

Dr. Altimose, while coming across very kind, cares little about her class or her student's success. Her tests are so difficult, that another professor commented to his class, "Be thankful y'all aren't taking Altimose's exam tomorrow." The slides aren't over the test material, and the lectures are useless. Take any other professor. Seriously.

By far the worst professor I've had! Although sweet, her lectures are very difficult to follow. I end up teaching myself the material and when preparing for the exam, her mock test is NOTHING like the exam. In addition to giving a short time limit on exams, she offers very limited resources to study and I truly wish I had taken another professor.

Totally unprepared to teach Chem 120. Lectures were unclear, and tests didn't match what was covered. She left for an international trip during a critical week (test & Q-drop) without advance notice or email support. The complete disregard for students' success was unacceptable. If you want a knowledgeable or caring professor, take someone else.

She is by far the worst professor I've ever had. She lectures horribly, does not know what she is doing a lot of the time. Her exams are absolutely awful 50x harder than other profs, nothing like the mock exams, quizzes, homework, or lectures. Take Martinez if I had him I would have a 100 i understand the course work but her exams are horrifying BS

This is genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. She cannot teach for her life and her exams are extremely hard. Try to take any other professor PLEASE. She will ruin your GPA and your dignity. She truly does not know how to teach in her lectures and will make every concept the hardest and most confusing it can possibly be. Just don't.

This professor is easily the worst I've ever had. Her GroupMe replies are polite, but that's where it ends. The quizzes and exams are absurdly difficult and barely related to her slides. She seems unaware of her own content. Honestly, I doubt she could pass her own tests. Take anyone else and save your sanity.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Dr. Altemose as a professor for this course. Attendance is mandatory but her lectures are unorganized and messy, and she often messes up her explanations in class, sending out emails later with the correct math or process. Her exams are also notoriously harder than other profs despite her subpar teaching.

Just don't. Dr. A is nice and responds fast in the class groupme but that's it. She doesn't know the content and cannot teach it well. She makes several mistakes while teaching and the notes are unhelpful. The exams and quizzes are significantly harder than any given practice problems. You will need to teach yourself. I couldn't recommend her less.

If you have the option to, DON'T. She is so sweet and even made a groupme for the class so that she can answer questions late. However, her content and notes are bad. In no way do they prepare you for her hard exams. Her exams are notoriously hard that even another prof told his class to be grateful they don't have her.

Just don't take her. She does not know the Chem 120 material, or at least she doesn't show that she knows it. She always makes mistakes and has to go back the next day to fix them. Tests and quizzes are 10x harder than what is done in class. Yes, she is a nice, giggly person, but that is it. If you take her, you will have to learn on your own.

Although Alicia is very accessible outside of class and cares about responding to students groupme messages, she is not a good professor for chem 120. She struggles with the material and tells us the wrong thing. Quizzes are also harder than practice problems given. Be prepared to learn from the SI leaders and youtube.

She is very nice and to say she doesn't care about her students would be a lie, however she seems unfamiliar with the material or just struggles to teach it. Attendance isn't mandatory but is graded and not by enough to outweigh quiz and test grades if you do poorly on them. Frequently explains problems wrong in class and gives super hard tests.

I began this class with high expectations for Dr. Altemose due to her reputation as a great professor for Chem 107, but when I came to Chem 120, I was incredibly disappointed. It seemed as if she either did not know or did not remember the content she was teaching in class. She continuously makes mistakes and shows a complete lack of understanding.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely do not take her for 120. She has no idea how to teach the course and every single day will solve the problems wrong in lecture and then send out an email late at night with an explanation on how to actually solve the problems. Her quizzes are impossible and tests make no sense. Useless office hours and mock exam. Terrible!!!!!!

No. She appears to not understand chem 120 and repeatedly gets questions wrong on lectures. Quizzes that are almost weekly are MUCH more difficult than any practice question done in lecture (which may or may not be done right the first try in class). I only did well in the class because I self studied with a study guide some other student made.

She seems very nice and wants people to do well but she is insanely unorganized. She's show us incorrect practice problems all the time and only correct herself via long emails. She's rude when you address her mistakes in class, and the learning lab she runs is even worse. More incorrect answer keys and tutors who are just as confused as us.

You will do a lot better off learning yourself from videos or SI or IA sessions. Her lectures are veryconfusing and not helpful, but she post typed up slides after that class of what you talked about that day. They are a lot more thorough and make more sense than following along with her in class. Her test are hard they're only 16 question multiple

She is an alright person, but her teaching style is definitely not for everyone. She also is the most difficult professor test-wise, as each 107 prof gets to write their own tests for whatever reason. She is also the only prof that had FRQs, and my grade tanked because god forbid I do an iota of math in my head. Take someone else if you can.

She is the only teacher who gives FRQs on the tests. Her lectures were difficult to follow and didn't explain concepts well. The class made it for you to succeed if you already knew chemistry and struggle heavily if you didn't.

People confuse her teaching skills with her kindness. She is caring and accessible outside of class, but she is a bad professor. She spends WAY too much time talking about her pets and ends up cramming too much in lectures. She's also VERY disorganized and has messy handwriting when working on problems. All your learning has to be outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade you get reflects the work you put in. I had no faults with Dr. A and I could've had a higher grade if I paid more attention in lectures. As a Prof, she is very approachable and friendly. For anybody not interested in Chemistry, 107 is going to be difficult no matter what.

The class itself is tough, regardless of the professor. Dr. A grades fairly and has fun lectures. Don't just do the iClickers and do other hw in class; actively listen to her lectures. You get exactly what you put in to this class. Heads up, quizzes are tougher than you think.

Dr. A is awesome. She keeps me engaged in classes by providing a picture of her cows/dogs at the start of the class! The best thing about her is that we have a groupme with all of her sections. Students are able to help each other out, but more importantly, Dr. A responds to a lot of questions herself in a really short time.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. A is the goat. She's very understanding and accommodating. The people complaining about the difficulty of the quizzes don't know how to study. They were very manageable and she drops the lowest one. She also rounded my 89 to an A after I did poorly on the final .People complaining about the mock exams are lowkey geeked they were very helpful

Prof. Altemose is a caring instructor who makes the material approachable. While quizzes can be challenging, staying on top of homework and using resources like Unstuck ai makes it manageable. Put in the effort and you'll likely secure a solid grade.

Dr. A was a very nice and caring teacher. Personally, I found most of her course managable to complete including the weekly OWL homework and occusional quizzes. There are also participation questions every class which count to your grade. Her first two exams were easy but her last exam was quite challenging. Still better than most others.

Dr. A is super accessible and her office hours were great. However, if you didn't take college level chem in high school - this class wont be easy. She speeds through lectures but posts them so you can catch up if needed. The exams were generally easy; however, the final is going to haunt me. Overall, not a bad class, just work hard.
She's not that great at explaining so sometimes you have to go learn on your own, but other than that she's fine.

She is very kind, but the class is insanely difficult. Two exams that weren't too bad, then a final that was very hard. The quizzes are online with Respondus, and they are very hard and worth 15%, so study for them. IClicker is 10%, so attend classes and don't skip. Overall a very nice professor with clear objectives, but be prepared to work hard.

Dr A is phenomenal! She's super sweet and fun and showed pictures of her cows/dogs before class and learned my name faster than any professor I've had so far. Though there's not extra credit, she had office hours/review sessions almost every day. The class itself was difficult but study and take advantage of her office hours and you'll be fine.

Flew through lectures and is overall a really terrible lecturer in my opinion. Her grading breakdown is nonsensical. We aren't able to view our grades on canvas which I do not see the point in whatsoever. She is kind though, but a bit passive when you ask questions. Her mock exams aren't helpful, so don't waste your time. Final was horrific.

Dr. A is probably one of, if not the most, accessible prof I've had all semester! She also made lectures fun with pet pictures (and sometimes demos) and brings an upbeat vibe to lectures. Attendance is mandatory via iClicker. 3 exams (last is cumulative final). This class is tough, but Dr. A provides mock exams and has extra practice + SI sessions.

If you pay attention during lectures and do the iClicker and Owl homework, getting an A is really doable. Dr. Altemose is super caring and understanding. There are 6 take home quizzes but the lowest is dropped. I got an A on the two exams but the final was much harder. Other than that, I really enjoyed the class.

She runs through the lectures like crazy but for most classes you have to self study so it's alright. She's super nice and provides a lot of resources to study but one thing I'd say is that she gives out practice tests and tells you that it doesn't mean you'll do good if you do well on them so what's the point of giving those practice exams.

Overall her lectures are informative and interactive with students. I had no personal dislike towards the professor other than the grading breakdowns. The quizzes are extremely difficult for students who haven't taken any prior college level Chemistry classes, and the exams are just as hard. Mock exams are way too easy compared to the real exam.

Professor Altemose is a great teacher! She encourages active note-taking in class while listening to the lecture. Clicker points are used to monitor attendance, but she offers "extra credit" assignments to make up for missed lectures. Quizzes are hard (lowest dropped), but not unreasonable. Make sure you review well before taking the test.

Her rating is way too low. Yes the class is hard if you haven't taken a chem class in awhile but Dr. A gives great feedback and lectures very well. She also cares about her students and how they are doing and she is very accessible outside of class. The only issue I had with her is that we were constantly behind but I don't think thats her fault.

Dr. Altemose is most likely one of the best professors I'll have during my time here. She breaks down every concept very thoroughly and genuinely cares about our learning. She is super sweet and engaging during lectures. You will learn a lot if you take her and apply yourself. She also does super cool experiments during class.

Dr. A is an amazing professor for a difficult class. She goes through pretty much every topic in class with examples and is very accessible outside of the classroom, having weekly review sessions. She is very understanding, and also has a class GroupMe where you can ask her questions about course material.
One of my best professors.

Great English, funny, slides were sufficient, lecture recordings were available.  Very approachable professor.  Take-home quizzes and take-home midterms were HARD.  Chemistry for Engineers is just Chemistry...with students who are Engineers...content includes orbital diagrams, molecular structures, thermodynamics, reaction rates, and other things.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. A is one of the sweetest professors ever! So approachable! The class itself is difficult, especially if you've never taken a chemistry course before. Dr. A hosts several in person and online office hours, practice sessions, and provides so many practice problems! Ask questions, go to office hours, and put in some effort and you should be good!

Dr. Altemose is an amazing professor, and is super caring and willing to help students if you seek it, although her lectures are rushed and overwhelming. Clicker questions are used for participation in class. Go to her office hours and attend SI/IA sessions and you will be fine, and don't underestimate the class!

She is always in a good mood in class which brightens everyone up!
Her lectures can be rushed sometimes, but you can always find her notes posted on Canvas (I find that her posted notes are better than in class.)
I got good understanding of the topics through the assigned homework. The quizzes and exams aren't too bad.
She tries to make the class fun and does a good job of teaching the content.

She's really nice but you mostly learn from homework. Lectures are just her reading directly off the slides and she'll rush important topics. I learned everything from the ALEKS homework. If you don't mind teaching yourself you'll do well. Participation is taken in every lecture by doing iClicker questions.

Class was the hardest class I took. Im bad at chemistry and didnt put much work into it. Shouldve ended with a C but somehow secure the B. Her quizzes are insanely hard and are proctored online. A lot of extra credit and very reasonable with extensions. She's honestly a great professor

Altemose was a very chill and caring professor. The class itself isn't that difficult but sometimes the quizzes can be weird and difficult, exams weren't terrible. Put in a little effort to study and it should be at least an easy B.

She is the GOAT. My favorite prof ever. She knew my name after I had only gone to a few office hours. The HW can sometimes take a while, but are manageable if you start early. The HW are the best way to learn. Dr. A really cares about the students, and you can always go to her with any problem you are having. 100% hope to have her in a later class.

She was a good lecturer and cares about her students. I wouldn't take her again but that's just me; I would still recommend her class. Be prepared to read the slides and know them well for quizzes and exams though.

Literally the sweetest human being on the planet. She's so nice and willing to help you if you reach out. Honestly, the only people I know who had a problem with this class are people who thought they could get by without studying or going to class (so, their fault not the professor's). If you put in the effort you'll be gucci.

I'm tempted to give her 1 star because of inflated her rating is in my opinion. Everyone left lectures visibly confused and her teaching style wasn't effective at all. Only went to class for iclicker, and learned through SI sessions and Professor Dave on youtube. You can barely see her in class "experiments" that also get no explanation. Annoying.

Dr. Altemose is an amazing professor for CHEM 107. She has engaging lectures and is a very approachable person for questions. She responds to emails very quickly and is happy to help. She teaches the material very well. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does use iClicker that is part of your grade. Lots of HW, two tests and 6 quizzes w/ one drop.

Dr. Altemose is a great professor and very accessible outside of class.Quizzes were the hardest part of this course but make sure to do the end-of-chapter problems and the homework and you should be good.The midterm and the final are easy if you prepare well (do A LOT of practice).
Definitely take Dr. Altemose if you can, she's the best.

The best part about CHEM107 with Dr. Altemose was the fact that she recorded every lecture and posts them on Canvas. Her lectures are helpful but not exactly engaging. The quizzes are easily the hardest part of her class, followed by the midterm and final; make sure to do well on those and you have an A.

Very easy class and teaches chemistry in a great way for those who are exposed to it for the first time. Attendance was mandatory in the sense that you had to complete participation activities while in class for a grade but other than that the class was great. Would reccomend.

She was really nice and definitely need to go to lectures for the clicker points and her clicker points are easy to get 100 on and provides extra credit. Everything was good except the quizzes are really heavy on grade so study for them, it was the only reason I got a B and not an A.

Really nice teacher, provides up to 3 bonus pts on semester avg from extra credit. Teaches a little bit slowly but that's honestly fine. She is always willing to help if you have questions. Quizzes are weighed an absurd amount so take those very, very seriously.
She is very kind. If you go to classes you should be fine. DON'T take your quizzes as a joke study for them.

Dr. Altemose is super nice, her lecture explains things very well, and she always willing to help students outside of class. She host help sessions very often. 6 quizzes, 2 exams. Don't skip classes, and you will be fine

Fun & passionate teacher. Has 6 sort of hard quizzes (lowest one dropped) & 2 tests (midterm and final). Quizzes & midterm are online & can be taken anytime during the day it opens. Final is also online. Very willing to help students outside of class. Records lectures and posts filled notes but uses iClicker to keep attendance up. Must study.

Great and passionate lecturer. Attendance is a good portion of your final grade. Weekly homework that takes quite a bit of time to finish but is great preparation for the five quizzes we have over the semester. Only a midterm and a final exam. Skipping lectures is an easy way to fall behind. Great feedback on quizzes and easy-to-follow lectures.

Super nice person, she's not the best lecturer as she's always a bit behind but she gets the job done. The class is fairly hard as not many engineers are good at chem but if you do average on quizzes/exams you should be fine.

Dr. A is a great prof to take for Chem 107. Her lectures start slow at the beginning of the year and speed up a lot towards the end. All quizzes are taken outside of class online and so is the first exam. She releases feedback on all the quizzes and is very caring and willing to help students. One of the best general chem profs.
She's nice and gives good material and not a crazy amount of work, I didn't get an A because I didn't take the class seriously enough which I regret but even with slacking off I still got a B+

This past semester was her first time teaching 117, she did a pretty good job. Her quizzes and exams have a good amount of tricks on them so even if you study and know curriculum, the chances of slipping up on major assignments is high.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Altemose is very sweet and caring! She genuinely wants you to succeed. However, her lectures always seem to drag on and on. We were always behind and then would have to cram lots of content right before the exam. The work load was pretty average and I didn't think the exams were too hard. Her office hours were helpful.
I only took her labs but the hw was unnecessarily hard. Quizzes were average. Group projects are graded pretty harshly so get a good group. show up to lab!!!

Lab requires a lot of work and there are many ways to get deduction on points. The syllabus and what is expected for grading is not clear. Some areas graders where harsher than others and then sometimes they were looking for specific answers. Overall, it is a lot of work and is fast paced for a one hour credit course. be ready for workloads .

I had her for the 117 lab and while the lab was fine, the HW was atrocious. There were no clear grading criteria, grades were hidden the entire semester, there was no instructions for the smart worksheets, and when they did provide instructions for projects, they focused almost entirely on formatting and almost nothing on expected content.

I had Dr. Altemose for CHEM-107, and she was a great teacher. There were 3 tests and a final where I received an 89 or above on all. At the beginning of the semester, she starts out very slow and speeds up ALOT at the end. Overall I couldn't have asked for a better Chemistry teacher and IA. When studying make sure to study the quizzes she assigns.

The class consists of a ton of lectures, and very difficult exams. She tells you what homework problems to study for the weekly quiz, which range from very helpful to near useless. Attendence is mandatory, and participating in class is also mandatory, as if you don't you'll likely do badly on the iClicker questions, which are graded.

Dr. Altemose was overall easy to follow but the pace of the course is a bit fast so it is difficult if you didn't take an advanced chemistry in high school. The lectures were a bit disorganized and Dr. Altemose did have trouble wrapping up her lectures in time and so the topics were often explained in a disjointed manner which was challenging.

The actual lab isn't too difficult but the SmartWorksheet assignments are absolute garbage. There is no room for error, if you accidentally press enter on your keyboard or make a slight typo your grade will drop. Make sure to get a great group.

The quizzes are way harder than the exams and the exams are fine as long as you study her mock exams. We still have 1 more exam and the final but I'm sitting at a B and don't think I'll drop down. It just depends on how much work you're willing to put in. Dr. Altemose is a little interesting but she's sweet, you can pass her with a decent grade.

This class really was the worst class in the first semester of engineering. The TA you have doesn't really matter. The labs are easy but SO LONG. Hope you have this later in the day because I would've hated to have this in the morning. The prelab and postlab work takes HOURS and every mistake you make on a quiz or hw TANKS your grade. (No final)
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr Altemose very intelligent and caring, but the structure of the class and her grading system made me struggle. Her lectures are not great as she reads off of slides and has a monotone voice. Lectures on are pretty useless for exams. You can't view your grade average without doing some math because the average is not posted on your Canvas.

She was very clear as to what to expect on exams making her class relatively easy. Her mock exams were almost identical to her actual exams. You will make an A if you study. 

Take her :)
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of example problems done in class. Only have to attend 70-75% of classes to receive full attendance points (assuming that you answer all clickers questions correctly on days you attend). Occasionally fell behind in lectures and sometimes would barely make it through all the material before tests. Stay ahead on ALEKS homework.

The professor and the TAs sent regular emails, and all of the grading guidelines were clear. The Chem 117 course itself is alright, but I appreciate Dr. Altemose's regular communication each week with reminders and explicit deadlines.

She has very clear grading criteria and as long as you meet that criteria, you will do well. All the labs are group projects. Before each lab, you have to complete the pre-lab assignments and quizzes. You will have SmartWorksheets over your labs and have to submit your lab notebook. It's a LOT of work for a 1 credit hour class.

The review is more for Chem 117, not Alicia Altemose (hence the 5-star rating). This class was absolutely awful. Assignments do not teach or demonstrate concepts. Assignments include doing the same calculation 90 times. Grading criteria are unclear and there is little to no feedback. I would recommend getting a waterproof notebook to be safe.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects
