reviews.comment: Dr. Altemose's class wasn't too difficult but you must commit outside of class. Attendance taken via iClicker. A lot of homework comes in from lab and it's tedious at times.  Mock exams are really similar to tests so if you can do those then you'll be fine. The only thing I'd say is she falls behind easily and has to skim through important things.

If you're self-sufficient, you'll do fine. Dr. Altemose is nice, but she spends a lot of time on announcements and iClicker, so we have to rush through some of the important exam material. She posts old lecture videos to watch at least. There is lots of homework on ALEKS and lab stuff to take care of, but time manage well and you'll be fine.

Altemose is a good person but her lectures are hard to understand. Half the time, I have to learn from Aleks even with that,  I do not learn enough. When I am in class, it's hard to understand her during her lectures. She reads off her slide and not explain it enough. The exams were not to bad. She posts mock exams . The SI & Zoom were helpful.

Although she may be a nice person, as a professor she isn't understandable as her lectures were very messy and unorganized. For example, she would skip over questions in class that would pop up on the exam and for her teaching she would literally just read off the slides word for word. She would also mess up on required iClicker questions answers.

I'm sure she's a nice lady, but her class is horrible. She required 3 different homework subscriptions, lectures were mandatory, yet made you even more confused so you have teach yourself everything, amount of homework was insane, not enough time given for long difficult tests, and she wouldn't cover all test material before tests.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Altemose is a super sweet lady and genuinely cares about her students. However, she is not at all a good teacher. I was able to do well in the class solely because I taught myself through ALEKS, generous exam prep, and remembered things from previous chemistries. Participation is graded so you still have to attend. Do not recommend!!!!!!!!

Prof is a very sweet lady and I can tell she cares about her students but her style of teaching is very odd. Attendance for her lectures is mandatory, but she teaches an insane amount of useless information that will not show up on exams. She skips over useful problems in class and makes students learn most things at home or through ALEKS (hw).

Dr. Altemose is one of the sweetest human beings ever, but her lectures only lead to confusion and do more harm than good. The only reason I am doing so well is because of the homework system and the mock exams that are provided. I have taught myself this entire semester. If you are a self learner, take her. If you are not, find another professor.

Very nice person but did not cover a single problem in class. She would lecture over things that were never tested on and you would have to learn the test problems on your own. Several problems that were never covered on homework or in class would be on the exams.  I have nothing against her as a person but don't take this teacher.

Dr. Altemose is an amazing person, but I could not for the life of me understand her work or the way she explained things. She gives practice exams before the exams but even with that its a lot of self teaching from Aleks. She also falls behind very easily so will skim over things that are very important material and it pops up on the exam.

Altemose is an OK prof. Very nice and generous when it comes to test prep, but her lectures can get hard to understand and most will find themselves learning 90% of the material on their own time. If you cannot teach yourself material, don't take her. Her exams are quite easy, with half MC and half FR, and practice exams help a lot.

lectures are useless,self taught everything from the videos she posted+hw modules.lots of time commitment needed outside of class. mock exams are useful and similar in content to the actual exam (she uses the same type of questions but asks you to solve for a dif variable).if you know how to do everything in the mock exam youre guaranteed an A.

I would not recommend this professor to anyone. She is genuinely a nice person but in my opinion she is not suited for the classroom. I had to go out of my way to get extra lessons from A+ tutoring and that's what really got me through the semester. Id say the only good thing about her class is she is a very easy tester and gives practice exams.

Very caring about her students and very accessible outside of class for those who need help. If you can do the mock exams, you'll do pretty well on the exams. Her lectures get confusing and chaotic at times, but she posts lots of additional material that help. Not my favorite teaching style but definitely one of the best chem professors available

My course was a guinea pig class for her new teaching method. Class was not organized and we were always behind in lecture. She is very kind and caring about the students, but I wish the class was more structured and on time so I wouldn't be pressured by the amount of information that is piling up.

Altemose was a very sweet professor, but she is new and I think is still trying to find her teaching style. I feel like in a couple years she will be a much more confident professor, but this semester was not bad at all. She is very adaptive and kind. ALEKS was not even that bad but literally every chem professor uses it so there is no escaping.

Dr. Altemose is not a great lecturer and we were always behind schedule with course material. Quizzes are harder than the exams, so be sure to study for those. There is only a midterm and a final which are easy because she gives you a review/ practice exam before each. Overall, an A is doable but it is a lot of self-teaching using ALEKS.

Very nice as a person, but extremely unorganized as a professor. Our class got 2 weeks behind the other chem classes bc she couldn't get through a lecture on time. Very hard to follow her work through a problem and the lessons never had much structure. You will learn more from ALEKS than from lectures. Coming from someone whos not great at chem:(

Dr. Altemose is such a sweet lady but would not recommend her as a professor. She seemed to not completely understand the chemistry topics herself which confused us students even more. Her teaching method is not very organized and her notes are a little confusing. Overall, she is an incredibly sweet lady but I would not recommend taking her course.

You can tell that Dr. Altemose clearly cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed in her class. She was always willing to go back and explain concepts that her students were confused on, but this did make her lectures pretty slow-moving. The homework was also very time consuming, and you needed to learn some material on your own time.

Dr. Altemose clearly cares a lot about her students; however, I found the class to be way too slow. We failed to cover all the material in class and had to watch lecture recordings to complete the homework. On a positive note, there are dropped quizzes, and the exams are similar to the reviews. She is also very easy to reach outside of class.

Dr. Altemose is new to teaching; that being said, she was not a great lecturer and never finished the material. She was difficult to access outside of class and expected us to watch hours of videos to keep up with the material on top of the ALEKS hw. However, the class is not hard to get a good grade in if you do the homework and teach yourself.

*online* Wasn't confident but she's a new teacher so didn't learn much from her. Homework was annoying but straightforward with unlimited tries. Lab depends on your TA but it's just a lot of busy work. Tests were easy enough as the quizzes show you the type of questions you will see. Clicker for class so make sure you show up a decent amount.

Dr. Altemose is clearly very knowledgeable, but struggles with time management. A LOT of learning on your own & work outside of class. That being said, if you do the ALEKS hw & study lecture slides & watch the videos she provides, you should be fine. She dropped 2 quizzes at the end which really helped

She's one of those profs who clearly doesn't want to be there. She was extremely slow during lectures and never finished them. She would then expect us to watch hours of videos over the topics she didn't get to in class. Aleks for homework is terrible - takes multiple hours each week and doesn't help you learn. 100 midterm and 88 final got me a B
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DrAltemose cannot teach. She often doesn't even know how to solve the problems herself. Her writing is illegible. She gives hours of homework per week on top of hours of lecture you are expected to watch on your own time. She is incredibly slow and not confident in herself. The only good thing I can say is she's passionate. I self-taught everything

Altemose is hands down the worst professor at Texas A&M. She is obviously only here for the free research. I got the majority of my knowledge from ALEKS, our homework software because she didn't know how to teach during lectures. There were multiple occasions she didn't know how to solve problems that she gave us, which would confuse us even more.

The class was set up nicely. Theres only a midterm and a final (no other tests). I like that part. The problem with her is her teaching style. I learned nothing in lecture all semester and taught myself 100% of Chem 119. You can tell she is passionate about chemistry, but she has no idea how to teach. Independent learners, take her. If not, DONT!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All of chem119 is literally a joke especially the labs. But Dr. Altemose is a new prof and Im not a fan of how Altemose lectures in class but she does give you all the materials you need to get an A in the class. She is so so sweet and caring and she definitely made chem a better experience for me.

This is just a chem lab, so it's taught by a TA. Overall, grading is pretty harsh and the workload is intense for a 1 credit hour class. Honestly, you really have to prepare before class to understand the labs and get the right results. Homework is tedious. Same applies to most CHEM117 classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Most of my knowledge of chem 119 stems from purely doing my ALEKS homework. I was not a big fan of Altemose's lecture methods (flipping through powerpoints during class); additionally, it took her at LEAST 15 minutes to begin teaching. Altemose is so nice and has a kind heart but I would not recommend- especially if you are not the best at chem :(

Honestly, CHEM 119 with Altemose was my most favorite class this semester! The class is easy if you show up to class and use her power points and videos to study for the quizzes and tests (which where pretty easy and basic). She's probably the best and easiest CHEM professor out there!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: the class is extremely confusing, she confuses herself when teaching us difficult questions. She is a very kind prof and cares a lot about her students and how we do, she just doesnt know how to teach the material all too well. Your learning is dependent on the aleks because during lecture you will not learn much. Good Luck
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is way too strict about assignments and due dates for a 1 hour class. Assignments are due bi-weekly, but for the one random time a quiz was due on an off-week, she had absolutely zero sympathy for those who did not get that quiz done on time and dropped our grade 4%. Do not expect her to be lenient and don't even try to reach out for help.

I will personally apologize in advance that you are forced to take Chem(Lab)117 as a freshman engineering major. Absolutely disgusting structure, not lenient on grading, and will surprise you with due dates. Pay close attention to weekly emails, and DO NOT procrastinate on any labs/prelabs. Don't bother emailing this prof, absolutely useless.

She doesn't start until over halfway to class and can never answer your questions. She gives a ridiculous amount of homework but doesn't teach you how to do it. However, she is a very nice person and you can tell she cares, she just isn't a good teacher, also her dog is super cute
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: she never starts lecture till halfway in the time so we never get through the metal, which makes the homework ten times harder. half the time she cant actually answer your question.

Altemose is probably the easiest professor you'll get. She moves at an extremely slow pace and pushes everything back. Only two tests all year and gives a review for them that are exactly like the test. She does take participation for a grade but I think every chem prof does this. Quizzes are very basic and labs are a joke. Take her if you can.

Dr. Altemose the amazing professors I have ever had! Honestly, if you do your work and prepare for her tests (there's only 2 :)! ) with the resources she provides, then the course shouldn't be very difficult. ALEKS takes time and it's not to bad. She is super kind and truly cares for your success. I really wish she was teaching CHEM 120!

Chemistry 117 is a weed-out class, and is especially horrible for students that will not use chemistry in their career. Be prepared to work hard for this class if you do not care about chemistry in the first place.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The quizzes and tests are pretty straightforward but I don't like how there are only 2 tests in the entire course so they weigh a lot on your final grade. There is a ton of homework, ALEKS is such a pain. Also we're constantly behind on the material and quizzes get pushed back every time. But easy labs, good lectures, plenty of office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Take Altemose for 119 if you can!! She is GREAT, chemistry can be a challenging class, and while her class isn't an easy A, she really helps and you can tell she wants her students to do well. She explains concepts super well and really prepares you for 120. An A is achievable as long as you go to class, take good notes, and study outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Altemose does a fantastic job of teaching difficult material. Unprepared students caused the lectures to deviate away from their intended purpose. There are no shortcuts, You are going to have to prepare ahead of class and do the work in order to do well in the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 2nd time taking this class, the 1st time I had a horrible professor. Altemose made ALL the difference! She is so caring and understanding. Her IA works really well with her. Together, they teach in a way that is very understandable. The only 2 exams were the midterm and final. There were 7 quizzes total and she takes the highest 5. Def take her!!!!

If youre like me & always struggled with chem then this will be a tough course but definitely not impossible. Dr. Altemose really helped me & our class in general on ensuring we had extra credit, review sessions, etc. Shes super sweet & worth taking if you have to take this on campus. Only had 2 exams (midterm + final) & 7 quizzes, 2 optional.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Altemose is one of the best gen chem professors at A&M. She is great at explaining the concepts and working through problems. If anything, she is a little too nice. A lot of class time was taken up reexplaining concepts that were supposed to be learned in the lecture videos posted before class. Mock exams are exactly like the test!

Chem will be difficult whatever prof you take, but if you can take this one. This was my second time taking chem119, & it was 100% easier to understand with Altemose. She is so kind & goes slow & steady during class and answers all questions! She makes herself available outside of class and offers much help. Be ready to put that work in for an A!

She is pretty new to teaching and it shows. Classes are not well structured, and not very productive as a result. If it were not for in class participation (reef polling) i probably wouldnt have attended, since lectures are recorded and meant to be watched before class (often posted too late as well). She might be better with more experience.

Dr. Altemose has been one of my favorite professors Ive had so far! I had to unfortunately q-drop chem last semester because I struggled with it so much, but thanks to Dr. Altemose I was able to do better this semester! Shes super helpful and is really understanding when it comes to deadlines.

Dr. Altemose is one of the most caring profs I've had at my time at A&M. She understands that situations come up and often moves back homework. Her lectures are very helpful and so are the SI sessions. The mind tap homework is quite a bit but you have a week to do it so its manageable. Exams aren't too bad and if you study you'll be fine!

Dr. Altemose is an amazing professor. She is very understanding with homework and will push it back if necessary. I think the main issue is she posts the lecture videos late in the day, so a lot of students don't have time to watch them. However, you do have a lot of things going into your grade so it is very easy to do well. Go to the IA's!

I basically learned everything from the textbook. Lectures were not very helpful nor clear (and posted late almost every week, expected to watch them the night before class). Way, WAY too much work and unclear instructions for assignments (especially with how the lab is organized!) Maybe take this class at Blinn if you can
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Altemose is one of the most caring professors I have gotten since I started here. Her class is hard but she makes sure to explain everything with clarity and answers any and all questions. She tries to makes lectures fun and gets her students to interact. Overall best professor in my opinion and would recommend, she made a scary class be fun.
Great Proffessor

The best chem 119 professors ever! She made every lecture easy to understand. Only had midterm and a final, but homework (ALEKS), reef participation question, and lecture quizzes boost your grade a lot. She is very helpful during the zoom lectures and will answer nearly ALL questions during the actual lecture. 100% recommend:)

She is the best professor ever!! If you have the opportunity to take her.. Do it! Chem 119 is already a difficult course but the professor is clear in her lectures and always responds to emails fast. She has such patience and does not mind questions. The whole class gave her the nickname of "queen" because she really is amazing!!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: lot of homework on Aleks with quizzes every few weeks and only midterm and final. you have to work and try to teach yourself on Aleks because lectures are repetitive and you solve very few practice problems in class. It wasn't that bad but you do have to work for it. Its chemistry and is difficult but just work on Aleks and read the book for help
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a very kind, knowledgeable, and patient professor. She is also good at explaining concepts & clear on assignments, but she does post her lecture videos, slides, and participation questions quite late at night (the night before class). Chem is not an easy class and the workload is crazy. However, work hard and you can definitely get an A.

CHEM119 is a difficult class for most people but Prof Altemose gives you the best opportunity to succeed. ALEKS homework was due 3 times a week and took up a lot of time but that's not really her fault. Exams were hard but there's only two and the practice tests and SI sessions were very helpful. Go to class, take notes and you'll do fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Altemose is super encouraging and very patient with us in class. She gives seven small scales quizzes instead of high steak exams and goes over review question and gives participation questions that are similar to the quizzes. This class definitely requires a lot of studying and staying on top of lectures and ALEK homework but is very doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: ALEKS was awful but other than that I have no complaints. Super sweet lady and makes chemistry super easy to learn.

Dr. Altemose was an awesome professor. She made chemistry super easy to understand, and she would always make time to meet with you during office hours or after class if you had any questions over the material. ALEKS can be a lot of work, but it's not too bad. She makes sure that her quizzes and exams only cover material that we've covered. 10/10.

ALEKS homework 3 times a week, and participation questions after class during class to make sure you attended the lecture. However, she is the most caring and understanding professor, she dropped the two lowest quizzes, and you can always ask her if you have trouble with a topic. Chem is hard, but she's teaches it well, just watch her lecture vids.

Alicia is a very caring prof that truly cares about her students. She loves chemistry and makes sure everything is understood about the material. There's a midterm, final, bi-weekly timed quizzes, homework every other day, and at least two lecture videos before the zoom class the next day. This class was time-consuming, hard and a lot of work.

Shes a great prof and is very caring. Gives lots of pts for HW and questions in class. Participation is very important every class. Make sure you have time before her class the day of because she posts lecture videos late the night before (between 5-12pm). There are 6 quizzes during the semester and a midterm. Lots of HW but its manageable.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This is by far my favorite prof at TAMU. She is kind, patient, and accessible, no matter how big your class is. If chem isn't your strong suit, take this course with Dr. Altemose. She is very understanding, just make sure to communicate with her. Make sure to take individual questions to her office hours instead of taking up everyone's class time!

Dr. Altemose is the sweetest professor I have ever had! She truly cares about her students and will answer any question you throw at her. This class has many opportunities for participation points. Turn on your camera during lectures, she loves to see her student's faces and go to office hours anytime, she is more than happy to clarify topics.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: take her. shes so sweet and her class is very easy to understand! you do have to purchase a homework subscription but it comes with the textbook. the lab is also very easy. just be sure to do the homework when its due, go to class if possible, and watch her lecture videos.
Shes not the best with online but shes a good professor if chemistry is not your strong suit

Chemistry is difficult but she made it easier to understand. She was very patient during office hours, even when she let me interrupt her lunch. Shes very approachable and nice which are great qualities for someone teaching a subject many students struggle in. Even during quarantine, she made herself available and gave review sessions for exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Solid prof. Tends to spend a little long on clicker questions but she wanted to make sure that everyone understood stuff. LOTS of homework throughout the week that can be easily forgotten so spend sometime on the weekend doing it to get ahead. Lectures include clicker questions for credit so make sure to show up. Would take again if she taught 120.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It was her first-semester teaching at TAMU and she did great. She is so sweet and passionate about chemistry. Very approachable outside of class. Cares about her students and their grades. Went above and beyond during COVID-19 to try and keep class normal. Practice exams are similar to exams and the syllabus shows a great break down of grades.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's super sweet and gives many chances to turn in work late! Most assignments are part of a larger grade chunk that doesn't need everything to be turned in in order to get full credit! Great choice
